cases.note: Two current authenticated results assert the same property and preserve both identities.
Two current authenticated results assert incompatible values for the same property; conflict must remain explicit.
Different policy versions have no implicit ordering merely because verifier identity matches.
Different trusted verifiers may provide compatible evidence over the same requested scope.
Expired evidence remains provenance-bearing historical evidence but does not contribute current assertions.
Selecting expired evidence as dominant current evidence is rejected.
Contradictory authenticated results cannot be collapsed into one value.
Composition whose outcome depends on arrival order violates the order-independent boundary.
Research-only negative assertions are retained as evidence and cannot silently disappear.
Evidence outside the required scope cannot satisfy a broader requested scope.
One result identity cannot name two different signed semantic contents.
Historical evidence needs an explicit historical identity and cannot silently re-enter the current evidence cut.
A count threshold remains aggregation metadata and is not an authorization grant.
Conflicting scientific interpretations must not be promoted into resolved fact by the composition layer.
Agreement is admissible while preserving both independent result identities.
An explicit conflict state is admissible when both valid result identities remain visible.
Deleting supporting evidence may remove an allow condition but must not create an allow from a deny.
Incomparable policy evaluations remain separately represented rather than ordered by recency or verifier name.
Exact replay of the same result identity and bytes is idempotent in semantic composition.
Incompatible scopes are preserved as incomparable evidence rather than choosing a scope winner.
